ingredients: ¼ cup (20 g / 0.71 oz) semisweet chocolate chips
⅓ cup (80 ml / 2.7 oz) spiced rum
⅓ cup (75 g / 2.6 oz) white granulated sugar
1 loaf (16 oz / 450 g) French bread or other non-sour white bread, preferably stale
steps: Soak chocolate chips with 2 tablespoons rum in a small container until needed.
Whisk eggs, cream, vanilla, remaining rum and 3 tablespoons sugar together.
Slice bread, trim crusts and cut into strips. Divide into thirds. Butter a loaf pan.
Peel bananas and halve crosswise, then lengthwise. Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add bananas and remaining sugar; cook 2 minutes per side.
Cover pan bottom with one-third of bread, half the bananas and half the chocolate chips. Add another third of bread.
Pour half the egg mixture into pan and let soak 1 minute.
Add remaining bananas, chocolate chips and bread, then remaining egg mixture.
Rest about 15 minutes while preheating oven to 350°F (175°C).
Bake 50 minutes, then cool 10–15 minutes. Serve with rum sauce, whipped cream or vanilla ice cream.

ingredients: Filling: ½ cup (100 g) white granulated sugar
steps: Prepare and bake Grandma's Pie Crust.
Whisk filling sugar, flour, salt and milk in the top of a double boiler until lump-free. Bring water below to a boil.
Stir constantly about 5 minutes until thickened. Cover and cook 10 more minutes, stirring occasionally.
Beat egg in a small bowl. Stir about ½ cup hot filling into the egg to temper, then return it to the hot filling. Stir constantly and cook 2 more minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in butter and filling vanilla.
Dip slices from 2 bananas in lemon juice, shake off excess and arrange in baked shell. Cover completely with half the filling. Repeat with remaining bananas and filling.
Chill about 1 hour.
Whip topping cream until peaks begin forming. Beat in topping vanilla and powdered sugar until peaks form, avoiding overbeating.
Spread whipped topping over chilled pie and keep chilled until served.
